(9) More Tools



APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(10) Just Use MCP?

  • The pitch: APIs are old, MCP is the future
  • Wrap anything in MCP → call it AI-ready
  • Skip the hard API work → straight to AI
  • Just start fresh after 10 years of API landscape work?


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(11) Problem 1: Directly Exposing APIs

  • Auto-generate MCP from OpenAPI
  • Context window explosion on real workloads
  • Bad descriptions → bad MCP
  • AI still has to invent workflows
  • Agents have poor API user experience


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(12) Problem 2: Investing in the MCP Layer

  • Hand-craft MCP servers, design good tools
  • The investment goes into the MCP layer
  • The capability layer remains untouched
  • Better capabilities benefit more than just MCP
  • Everybody's experience (UX/AX) should benefit


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(13) MCP-Washing

  • Skip the API work → jump to MCP → call it AI-readiness
  • Wrong place to invest from a strategy perspective
  • MCP should be a thin layer, not a fat one
  • Invest in your APIs and then expose them through MCP


APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(14) Better Described Tools



APIs and AI: A Possible Path Erik Wilde: API Conference Welcome and API Standards in the Age of AI

(15) Better Descriptions ⇏ Scalable Tool Use

  • Better AX reduces confusion and misuse
  • But even well-described tools still overload agent context
  • The problem shifts from understanding tools to finding the right ones
  • Composing APIs into workflows can produce better tools
